consuming_workflow: Manual read-only inspection of an existing native Project through View/Fit and truthful availability of three currently unimplemented menu actions.
intent: Expose supported actions only through context-eligible production consumers and prove actual native behavior separately from implementation, review and owner acceptance.
scope: Linux/X11, 1280x768 at scale 1.0, isolated native input and accessibility bus; verified GUI and CLI binaries from the recorded inputs with EDA_CLI_BIN pinned to the verified CLI (no implicit Cargo fallback); view.fit, view.layers, window.documents and help.about on their existing menu pointer/row-keyboard paths and the editor F/f shortcut. Missing handlers stay unavailable. This is a candidate G01 contract, not enrollment or runtime proof.
exclusions: No Preferences/Units redesign or acceptance, authored geometry, new panel/About functionality, new dependency, prototype edit, gate activation or broader platform acceptance. No restoration of the removed side-panel Fit button. No full-application keyboard-only accessibility claim: existing menu-row keys are tested after pointer opening; an additional menu-entry shortcut requires reviewed scope. Existing layer toggles, document navigation and other supported actions must not be disabled to pass this pilot.

scenarios.preconditions: Fresh identified candidate binary, normal launch with the archived native Project copied to scratch, private X11/accessibility session, 1280x768 scale 1.0. Focus Board and select one existing pad; record stable selection and pane identities. Record initial source/journal hashes and camera.
inputs: Wheel up twice over the focused Board to establish visibly non-fitted geometry; click View then Fit to Board.
Wheel up twice again over Board; with editor focus restored after menu activation, press unmodified F without clicking canvas geometry.
Wheel up twice again; click View, use Up/Down to focus Fit to Board, then press Enter.
scenarios.expected_visible: All three paths restore the same fitted Board view from a visibly zoomed view; no false success or unrelated dialog.
scenarios.expected_state: Each path reaches the same registry-backed datum_gui::Runtime::fit_camera identity. Zoom becomes 1.0 and camera center equals CameraState::fit_to_bounds for the recorded scene bounds. Selection, other-pane cameras, layout, source and journal remain identical.

scenarios.preconditions: Archived fixture includes an empty schematic (no sheets); establish and record the normal Board plus unresolved schematic placeholder context through existing View / Layout: Board + Schematic. Candidate must identify focused pane and whether it has a resolved camera; no test-only context injection.
inputs: Zoom Board with two wheel-up events, then open View and press Escape; press F after dismissal.
Use Tab to focus the schematic placeholder; open View and inspect Fit; attempt Enter on Fit, then dismiss with Escape.
Return to Board with Shift+Tab; zoom and invoke F; check each missing-consumer row remains unavailable after these focus changes.
Use the existing View / Fill Pane: Schematic and Fill Pane: Board entries to change the focused pane content; repeat readiness inspection and Escape dismissal without touching Project source.
scenarios.expected_visible: Escape dismisses the menu and leaves visible focus usable. Fit is enabled for the resolved Board, unavailable with its contract reason for the unresolved placeholder, and usable again on return. Missing consumers do not become enabled because focus changed.
scenarios.expected_state: No Fit invocation in an unresolved camera context, no successful no-op, and no refit of another pane. Menu dismissal returns keyboard ownership to the focused editor. Apart from explicitly requested pane/focus/camera view changes, selection, source and journal are unchanged.

requirement_refs.marker: ## How it rides the substrate (why this is Datum-shaped)

scenarios.preconditions: Same Linux/X11 candidate with a working private native accessibility bus. Production menu nodes must be observable; absent nodes or bus failure block proof, never justify N/A. Menus are pointer-opened because a keyboard-only menubar entry is not established by current production code.
inputs: Click View; collect the live accessible menu/row identities, labels, focus, enabled/sensitive states and unavailable reasons alongside the rendered menu.
Use Down/Up to visit Fit and Layer Visibility; record accessible focus/state after each key, then press Enter on the unavailable row.
Repeat row navigation/refusal for pointer-opened Help / About Datum and Window / Documents; press Escape and verify editor focus and F operability.
Change focused content Board to unresolved schematic and back through the existing pane controls; repeat View accessibility observations and confirm Fit availability changes with the rendered row.
Inspect that existing Terminal and Preferences accessibility objects are not replaced by menu objects; no setting change is made.
scenarios.expected_visible: Focus is visibly locatable; disabled rows remain inspectable and explain their unavailability without invoking their actions. Escape releases the menu and the supported Board F shortcut works. Keyboard-row behavior and native accessible states agree with paint.
scenarios.expected_state: Real native menu nodes expose stable identity/label and correct enabled, sensitive, focused and reason information from the shared readiness state. Unavailable rows never expose executable success; state changes follow actual input/context. No phantom menu nodes after dismissal, no replacement of existing accessibility consumers, and no source/journal mutation.
